image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a lionfish (Pterois) resting on a sandy and rocky seabed. The fish displays characteristic red, white, and brown vertical stripes. Its dorsal spines are elongated and fanned out, resembling a mane. Large, fan-like pectoral fins extend laterally, showing intricate ray structures. Pelvic fins are visible beneath the body. The background consists of blurred coral or rock formations.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Laterally compressed body with moderately sized proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape appears laterally compressed (thin from side-to-side, tall from top-to-bottom), consistent with lionfish anatomy. Proportions look natural for the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows the diagnostic vertical banding pattern in reddish-brown and white/cream colors across the body and fins.

While lionfish have small scales, the resolution and lighting of this specific image make individual scales indistinguishable from the general skin texture and stripe pattern. It is not possible to definitively verify 'small scales' vs smooth skin at this zoom level.
